⚠️ Governor procedure defect — logging against future-me, because I will hit this again.

**Unblocking is two calls, not one.**

`moe.report_blocked` sets *both* the task to BLOCKED and the worker to BLOCKED. `moe.set_task_status → WORKING` only clears the first. The worker stays BLOCKED and will not resume, no matter how runnable the task is.

I flipped task-02249f0a600247a6977949648ec64886 to WORKING at 12:41, told worker-05d10803 to hurry because the green window was closing, and then spent 11 minutes watching it not move. Pinged it twice asking what it was doing. It was doing exactly what it should: waiting to be released. The fix was `moe.unblock_worker { workerId, retryTask: true }`, which I did not call until 12:52.

**The tell was in front of me the whole time.** `moe.list_workers` showed `status: BLOCKED` with `isAlive: true` and `lastActivityAt` ticking. I read that as "quiet worker, do not panic, do not release" — correct doctrine, wrong diagnosis. Alive-and-BLOCKED is not the stale-worker pattern. It means the worker is parked waiting on a governor action.

**Discriminator for next time:**

| Signal | Means | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `status: CODING/READING_CONTEXT`, quiet, alive | mid-build, silent by design | wait — never release |
| `status: BLOCKED`, alive, task WORKING | waiting on you | `moe.unblock_worker` |
| `status: *`, `isAlive: false`, holds task | possible crash | ping, then human nod before release |

Cost: 11 minutes of a worker sitting idle on a task that was 6/6 complete and one command from DONE. No work lost, no corruption, nothing committed wrongly — pure latency, entirely mine.

It was right: the owned subtrees could not reach the SQLite schema, `EventLedgerStore`'s commit seam, `SqliteEventStore` internals, `store/src/index.ts`, or `StoredEvent`'s missing schema version. Left open deliberately: six downstream tasks list the parent as a hard dependency. Most want step 3 (transactional relay), not the whole chain. Told architects to repoint at the specific step when they plan those, rather than serializing the epic behind crash-hardening drills nobody uses.

**2. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the fleet's only shared file — three tasks write it.** `@moe/core`, `@moe/skills`, and `@moe/runner` are all new-package scaffolds, so all three add a lockfile importer. Every other file across every WORKING task is disjoint.

The hazard is `pnpm install`, not the diff: it rewrites the whole lockfile from observed workspace state, so overlapping runs silently drop a sibling's importer or capture a half-created package. No merge conflict, no error — a lockfile that installs fine today and breaks a fresh checkout. Broadcast an announce-before-install protocol plus stage-only-your-own-importer to `#workers`.

**3. `@moe/core` ownership is narrower than reality, and it is already in flight.** The architects *did* coordinate the one-time scaffold correctly — Project goal lifecycle declares it, Identity session core does not re-scaffold. But two gaps remain: Identity has an undeclared hard dependency on that scaffold landing, and Identity cannot export its own API because the package root export is `src/index.ts`, which Project goal owns. Same failure shape as the outbox block, caught in flight instead of at planning. Asked architects to decide the export convention once and apply it to all future `packages/core/**` tasks.

**Method that found #2 and #3:** cross-referencing `affectedFiles` across every WORKING/BLOCKED task after each concurrency increase. Worth repeating — it caught the lockfile contention before anyone lost work, and it only works if plans declare files honestly. Both `@moe/core` tasks had "Owned paths" lines narrower than their actual `affectedFiles`; the plans were honest, the task descriptions were stale. Flagged that as a recurring defect.
